analysis.description: The paper presents a policy iteration approach to batch reinforcement learning using continuation methods. It aims to address challenges in policy optimization by gradually relaxing constraints between the learned and behavior policy, employing KL regularization for better policy evaluation and utilizing continuation methods to help escape local optima.

type.justification: The paper presents results from experiments across various control tasks and environments, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed methods empirically.
type.quote: We present results on a variety of control tasks, game environments and a recommendation task to empirically demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method.

name.justification: The paper is primarily focused on reinforcement learning, particularly in the context of batch reinforcement learning and policy optimization under this setup.
name.quote: Many real-world applications of reinforcement learning (RL) require the agent to learn from a fixed set of trajectories, without collecting new interactions.
